title: Inside the Proud Tek Factory — RFID Manufacturing
summary: A walk through the physical plant behind Proud Tek's RFID products: two Shenzhen sites, ten automated lines and 305+ pieces of process equipment, plus an in-house test lab that proves every SKU — wash-cycle, read-range, environmental and mechanical — before it ships. This page covers the floor, the equipment, the material supply chain and the production-to-dispatch workflow; the capability overview and chip support live on the main About page.
heroPoints: Two Shenzhen production sites, ten automated lines and 305+ pieces of process equipment — assembly, lamination, printing, encoding and test under our own roof.
In-house test lab: laundry wash-cycle tunnel washer, UHF read-range range, plus environmental and bend/flex checks — SKUs are proven before they ship.
Every unit gets a 100% functional read test; the production traveler and test report are retained seven years for full lot traceability.

sections.title: Production capacity by line
sections.intro: Capacity is reported here as line-count and shift coverage, not weekly piece-count — RFID throughput depends almost entirely on the encoding scheme and the chip family in play, not on raw machine speed. We post conservative committed capacity per program once chip allocation is confirmed.

sections.title: On the production floor — plant and equipment
sections.intro: The main About page lists what we can make; this is where it physically happens. Ten lines are split across two Shenzhen sites and run by our own operators — the same crew builds the pilot lot and the production order, which is why first-run defect rates stay flat across a program's life.

features.title: Two sites, 305+ machines
features.text: Assembly is concentrated at one site, finishing and encoding at the other — 305+ pieces of process equipment in total, from chip bonders to reel-to-reel programmers. No value-added step is subcontracted to a job shop.

features.title: ESD-controlled assembly
features.text: Wet-inlay bonding runs at ESD-controlled stations with wrist-strap and ionized-air discipline — bare chips and thin-film antennas are static-sensitive. Conductive-adhesive cure temperature and dwell time are logged per lot.

features.title: Anti-metal & specialty line
features.text: A dedicated ferrite-backing line for on-metal IT-asset, tool and equipment tags. Read range against steel and aluminium is validated per SKU and filed with the production traveler — the specialty work most trading companies cannot do.

features.title: Reel-to-reel encoding hall
features.text: High-volume UHF inlay programs run on reel-to-reel encoders with inline read-test, so multi-million-unit orders are programmed and verified in one pass rather than hand-fed unit by unit.

features.title: In-house test lab
features.text: A tunnel washer for laundry-tag wash-cycle testing, a UHF read-range range for distance and orientation checks, plus environmental and bend/flex rigs. SKUs are proven against their real duty cycle before the pilot ships.

features.title: Bonded warehouse
features.text: Finished goods stage in a bonded warehouse that runs distributor safety-stock and scheduled call-off programs — call-offs typically ship within 3-5 business days of release authorization.

sections.title: Materials and supply chain
sections.intro: We treat material sourcing as a quality lever, not a cost lever. The inlay roll-stock, PVC sheet, conductive adhesive and ferrite backing are all qualified vendors with parallel sources for risk mitigation.
bullets: Inlay substrates — PET / PI roll-stock qualified from two parallel vendors; cut-sheet inlays inspected for thickness and dimensional stability before line entry.
Card stock — PVC, ABS, PETG, recycled-PVC; FSC-certified paper and bamboo composite stocks available on request.
Conductive adhesive — silver-loaded epoxy from named vendors; cure cycle validated per chip family.
Ferrite backing — automotive-grade ferrite sheet for on-metal SKUs; tested against representative steel and aluminum substrates.
Chip allocation — direct allocation channels with NXP / Infineon / Impinj / Alien / EM; authorized-distribution backup for spot demand.

sections.title: The test lab — proving SKUs before they ship
sections.intro: A 100% functional read test catches encoding faults, but a tag also has to survive its real duty cycle. Before a pilot is signed off, the relevant SKUs go through the in-house test lab against the conditions they will actually meet in the field.

rows: Survival across 150-200 industrial wash cycles at up to 95°C with chemical exposure
Read distance, orientation sensitivity and null zones against representative surfaces
UHF inlays, on-metal asset tags, retail source tags
100% functional read on every encoded unit; decode-rate and UID / NDEF verification
Temperature and humidity exposure; adhesion and peel for label stocks
Bend, flex and torsion endurance; delamination resistance

callout.label: Ask for the test data
callout.text: For a qualified program we can share the read-range plots, wash-cycle survival counts and AQL inspection results for your shortlisted SKUs as part of the sampling pack — useful when your own QA needs evidence before a production commitment.

sections.title: From PO to dispatch — production workflow
sections.intro: Once a production order is released, the program runs to a documented traveler. Every step generates a record retained in the quality archive for at least seven years per ISO 9001 requirement.

items.label: Day 0 — PO received, traveler issued
items.text: Production traveler issued with chip allocation, encoding scheme, artwork files and packaging spec locked. Material kit pulled from stockroom; raw-material lot numbers attached to the traveler for full traceability.

items.label: Days 1-5 — Assembly and lamination
items.text: Wet-inlay assembly or card lamination runs to the traveler. First-piece QC at line start, then in-process AQL sampling. Reject rate logged; out-of-spec lots quarantined before the next step.

items.label: Days 6-10 — Encoding and marking
items.text: Encoding station runs the locked scheme. Every encoded unit gets a functional read test; failed units rejected at the line. Laser engraving, hot stamping or print runs as specified.

items.label: Days 11-14 — Final QC, packaging, dispatch
items.text: AQL final inspection on visual and dimensional attributes. Packaging per spec; box-level barcode / RFID outer-pack labeling if requested. Shipment release after document pack (CO, COC, packing list, test reports) is signed off by QA.

sections.title: Customer audits and factory visits
sections.intro: We welcome buyer audits — they reduce procurement risk on both sides. The list below covers what we typically accommodate; non-standard audit scope (third-party social compliance, environmental, IT security) is scoped per program.
bullets: Buyer engineering audits — open access to wet-inlay, lamination, encoding and QC lines, by appointment.
Quality system audits — ISO 9001:2015 document review, training records, calibration logs, corrective-action archives.
Third-party audits — TÜV, SGS, Intertek, Bureau Veritas and BSCI / Sedex visits accommodated when the program requires them.
Pre-shipment inspection — buyer or buyer's QC agent can attend final AQL inspection in-house at no additional charge.
Virtual factory tour — live video walk-through available for buyers who cannot travel; we schedule against your time zone.

callout.label: Audit accommodation
callout.text: If your organization has a specific audit framework (Sedex, BSCI, Higg Index, RBA, FSC chain-of-custody, etc.) mention it on the initial inquiry. We can route the certification path and absorb the audit cost as part of an annual-volume agreement when justified.

sections.title: Compliance documentation shipped with every order
sections.intro: Every shipment leaves Shenzhen with the documentation buyers actually need at customs and at brand-owner intake. Certified third-party test reports can be commissioned on a per-program basis.
bullets: Commercial invoice and packing list with chip family, SKU code and encoding lot per line item.
Certificate of Origin (Form A / GSP / FORM E / Form F) per destination market.
Certificate of Conformity for radio compliance (FCC / CE / MIC / CCC as applicable).
Material declarations — RoHS, REACH SVHC, California Prop 65 on file by SKU.
Functional test report — sample lot of encoded units with read-range and decode-rate data.
ISO 9001:2015 certificate copy on request; recertification cycle dates publicly traceable.

faq.question: Can you test tags against our specific duty cycle before we commit?
faq.answer: Yes. The in-house test lab runs wash-cycle testing (tunnel washer, 150-200 cycles at up to 95°C), UHF read-range, environmental and bend/flex checks. For a qualified program we validate the shortlisted SKUs against your real conditions during sampling and share the read-range plots and survival data before you place a production order. (For minimum order quantities, see the FAQ on the main About page.)

faq.question: Can you handle multi-million-unit annual programs?
faq.answer: Yes. Multi-million-unit annual UHF inlay and HF card programs run on dedicated reel-to-reel encoding lines with 24/7 shift rotation when needed. Chip allocation is confirmed before commitment; we do not promise capacity that depends on a chip family we cannot lock in.

faq.question: How do you handle chip allocation when global supply is constrained?
faq.answer: We maintain direct allocation channels with NXP, Infineon, Impinj, Alien and EM, plus authorized-distribution backup for spot demand. During constrained periods (e.g., 2021-2022 MIFARE shortages), we communicate allocation availability up front and offer chip-substitution paths where the deployment context allows.

faq.question: Are buyer factory visits welcome?
faq.answer: Yes. We welcome buyer engineering audits and pre-shipment inspection — both reduce procurement risk on both sides. Visits are scheduled by appointment; we accommodate buyer's QC agents on-site at no charge. Virtual tours are available for buyers who cannot travel.

faq.question: What is included in the compliance documentation pack?
faq.answer: Every shipment ships with: commercial invoice, packing list, Certificate of Origin per destination market, Certificate of Conformity for radio compliance (FCC / CE / MIC / CCC), RoHS / REACH SVHC material declarations, and a functional test report on the encoded lot. Third-party test reports (TÜV, SGS) can be commissioned per program when needed.

faq.question: How long are quality records kept?
faq.answer: Production travelers, encoding logs, QC records and material certificates are retained for at least seven years per ISO 9001:2015 documented-information requirements. Records can be pulled by SKU code or encoding lot if a buyer needs traceability for a field issue or audit.
